seo.description: Cap Spartel is the headland west of Tangier where Atlantic and Mediterranean waters meet — lighthouse, cliffs and open sea air.

overview.title: The north-west corner of Africa’s Mediterranean edge
overview.p1: Cap Spartel marks the meeting zone of Atlantic and Mediterranean waters west of Tangier. A lighthouse stands on the headland; cliffs and wind define the stop more than a long walk network.
overview.p2: Most visitors combine it with the Hercules Caves in one half-day taxi loop. Bring a layer — exposure is real even when the city feels mild.

food.title: Eat on the cape loop
food.p1: Limited services at the cape itself — plan tea or a meal in Tangier, or ask your driver about simple stops on the road.
food.li2: Return to Tangier for a proper meal.
food.li3: Occasional cafés on the approach road.
food.li5: Combine with caves to save transfers.

1.title: Getting there
1.desc: Petit taxi or organised half-day with Hercules Caves; agree the round-trip price and waiting time.

2.title: Wind
2.desc: Exposed headland — secure hats and light layers.

3.title: Time needed
3.desc: A photo and walk stop, not a half-day hike.

q1.question: How far from Tangier?
q1.answer: About 20–30 minutes by road west of the city.

q2.question: Can I go inside the lighthouse?
q2.answer: Access rules vary; the outdoor viewpoint is the main visit for most travellers.

q3.question: Combine with Hercules Caves?
q3.answer: Yes — the standard half-day loop from Tangier.

q4.question: Is it worth it in bad weather?
q4.answer: Wind and fog reduce the experience; clear days are far better.

q5.question: Entrance fee?
q5.answer: Outdoor areas are generally free; any lighthouse or parking fees are local and small.
